_comment: Named feature combinations. Schema and rules: contrib/perf/docs/SCHEMA.md S4. A bundle is a NAME for a feature set, not a substitute -- both are stored on every row. Never redefine an existing bundle: add a -v2 instead, or old rows silently change meaning. Bump bundle_v when adding. bundle_v 3 adds HASH_BACKEND and EQUIHASH_BATCH_HASH: before it, a uniblake build and a libsodium build produced identical bundle keys.

stock.description: What ships to users. The default comparison baseline.

perf.description: Lab instrumentation build (--enable-perf). Root-latch counters and the block-file read latch compiled in, both off at runtime.

perf-fdcache-on.description: perf build with the block-file read latch enabled at runtime.

noteidx.description: Stock build, NOTEIDX witness path enabled. Iterates note-bearing txs only.

ibd-defer.description: Stock build, per-block witness build skipped during IBD and rebuilt after import.

uniblake-batch.description: Stock build with the Equihash batch list-generation path compiled in (EQUIHASH_BATCH_HASH). Default off.

architectural.meaning: Stable, long-standing ecosystem choices. Effectively constant across ZeroPerf scenarios and not expected to vary between batches. Recorded for completeness; NOT part of bundle matching, so a ZMQ-enabled and ZMQ-disabled build of the same perf configuration still compare as the same bundle.

scenario.meaning: Compiled default AND a runtime equivalent (-disablewallet; -gen/-genproclimit). Vary between batches of test scenarios and show up in ZeroPerf work often. Both the compiled capability and the runtime state are recorded, because a wallet-capable binary run with -disablewallet is NOT the same measurement as a binary built without wallet support.

perf.meaning: ZeroPerf lab instrumentation. Off in shipped builds. Always part of the bundle key.

hash.meaning: Which BLAKE2b implementation Equihash hashes through, and whether the batch list-generation entry point is compiled in. Part of the bundle key: two builds differing only in the hash backend are not the same measurement, and pooling them would average different code paths.
